messages:
sara: Quick sync — we need a minimal contract for new runtime sensors that cover SM occupancy, SM memory, and per-pool queue_depth for both Hosted and Dedicated. Goal: dashboards + alerting + routing policy inputs.

ajay: Agree. can we define metric names and cardinality up front? otherwise dashboards explode.

maria: Proposed names: `redwood.sm.occupancy_pct`, `redwood.sm.memory_bytes_used`, `redwood.sm.queue_depth`. Add labels: pool_id, pool_type(hosted|dedicated), host, gpu_card, model_shard. Thoughts?

tom: +1 on names. keep pool_type low-cardinality. model_shard might be high-card — do we actually need it on dashboards? maybe only for debug mode.

sara: Good call. dashboards should default to pool-level aggregates (pool_id, pool_type). Shard-level can be optional sampling.

neil: For ingestion: what sampling rate and push frequency? we should avoid 1s scrapes across thousands of cards. Suggest 5s for occupancy, 15s for memory, 30s for queue_depth by default.

ajay: Queue depth can be event-driven too — increment/decrement on enqueue/dequeue and emit occasional absolute snapshot. reduces churn.

maria: That works. Add a `metric_type` label: gauge vs counter for clarity. occupancy & memory = gauge, queue ops = counter + snapshot gauge.

sara: UX/console needs: per-pool heatmap for occupancy, timeseries for memory with percentiles, and a stacked bar of queue depth by priority. Also a small per-route quota delta panel (expected headroom vs committed).

tom: On routing policies: the router will consult occupancy_pct and queue_depth to decide spillover. We need SLOs: occupancy > 85% or queue_depth > 20 triggers conservative routing. Who owns those thresholds?

neil: That should be configurable per-customer but defaults live in eng-platform. We should store thresholds in config service and surface in Console under pool settings.

ajay: Action item: eng-runtime implements metrics + labels, eng-infra ensures ingest pipeline tags pool_type correctly, eng-platform builds dashboard and config UI, eng-sre defines default thresholds and alerts.

maria: I pushed a proto of the prometheus exposition format to the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcdef — snippet: ```# SM occupancy (gauge) redwood_sm_occupancy_pct{pool_id="p-123",pool_type="hosted",host="h1",gpu_card="gpu0"} 73.4```

sara: Nice. ingest-bot: can you create a telemetry ticket to onboard these metrics to metrics-ingest with those sampling rates?

ingest-bot: ticket created: METRICS-3107. assigned to eng-infra. :white_check_mark:

tom: One more: retention/rollup strategy. We should store 5s raw for 48h, 1m rollup for 30d, 5m rollup for 90d. Agree?

neil: Yes. And keep 90th/95th percentiles for occupancy/memory in rollups.

ajay: Also add a cardinality cap: if model_shard is enabled sampling only 1% of shards by default and tag sampled_shard=true. avoids high-card cost.

maria: Note for Dedicated: some customers will turn on full-shard telemetry. we need a flag per-tenant that bypasses sampling. include that in the contract.

sara: Summary of decisions and owners:
- Metric names & labels: agreed (maria)
- Sampling rates & ingestion TODO (neil + eng-infra)
- Router thresholds stored in config service + defaults (eng-platform + eng-sre)
- Dashboards & Console panels (eng-platform)
- Ticket created METRICS-3107 (ingest-bot)

sara: Next step: eng-runtime to post a small PR with producer-side snippet and a smoke endpoint we can point ingest to. Can you target EOD Friday?

ajay: I can do the PR. will include example exporter and opt-in sampling flags.

tom: I'll stub dashboard tiles and link to METRICS-3107, then we can iterate after raw data lands.

maria: I'll update the gist with the counter/gauge examples and the optional labels doc.

sara: thanks all. keeping this thread as the canonical convo. :thumbsup:
